quote: I do want to just double check with my manager and make sure we are able to help.
stewart_read: Rep did not know how to resolve a tenant-paid-meter edge case and admitted it via a manager check rather than guessing or fabricating an answer — the admit-and-recover path, not a fabrication. The customer's hostile reaction was to the WAY it was delivered (framed as a possible disqualifier) more than the check itself.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep should have recognized sole-ownership as an obvious pass and never floated disqualification language at all, since the customer clearly owns the entire building.
coaching_implication: Coach the framing, not the check itself: lead with the likely-fine read ("Since you own the whole building this should be fine, let me just confirm quickly") instead of opening with doubt, which reads as a stall to a customer already primed for scam suspicion.

quote: Yeah. Right. I'm just a a scheduler, so I don't really know a bunch of the specifics. Right?
stewart_read: This is the correct scope-holding line, but it arrived on the FOURTH attempt at the same ownership/cost question, after three earlier answers (bill swap explanation, ownership vs. leasing options, 'equipment isn't free') that each invited another round.
coaching_implication: Deploy the escape hatch on touch one or two, not four. Earlier partial answers extended a cost conversation the setter isn't equipped to have and that belongs entirely to the specialist.

quote: I got 600,000 to put solar on the resort right now. So I'm trying to figure out what's gonna be my best plan.
stewart_read: Customer disclosed a large-scale commercial/international solar buying intent (resort in Belize, apartment portfolio, $600K budget) that is entirely outside Ion's residential single-family/multi-unit script. The schema has no defined signal or routing path for B2B/commercial disclosures — this is a genuine schema gap, not a rep execution failure.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: does Ion have any commercial/multifamily-at-scale sales path, or is this pure out-of-scope noise? If commercial referral exists, this call shows a missed hand-off opportunity worth defining in the schema.

quote: That should be something you're aware of. This time, but I drive a Tesla, so it gets a little bit
stewart_read: Customer volunteers she drives a Tesla and charges it at home — a classic higher-electric-load signal that materially strengthens the case for a larger system. The rep acknowledged it socially ("running those bills up, I bet") but never anchored it as a design/value point for the specialist.
coaching_implication: Note EV charging explicitly in the specialist handoff notes as a load driver — it wasn't captured as a design consideration, only as small talk.

quote: Last month, I did 43. In the current month, I did 25.
stewart_read: The actual bill graph shows 25-43 kWh months, starkly lower than the customer's earlier verbal estimate of $181.80/month and her later claim of ~30 kWh/month or $189 winter bills. The rep noted the bill "is definitely a little bit lower" but didn't flag the discrepancy as a reason to get accurate data before the appointment, nor use it to build curiosity about what the real design number would show.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have judged that reconciling the discrepancy live wasn't necessary since the specialist will build the design from the actual bill photo, not the verbal estimate — the photo capture itself resolves the accuracy question.
coaching_implication: When stated bill and actual usage diverge this much, name it directly to the customer ("this graph's lower than what you quoted — is this a slower month, or should we look at winter bills too?") rather than letting it pass as a minor aside; it's a live curiosity-building moment, not just a data hygiene issue.

quote: Looking through my schedule, we've actually got tomorrow afternoon. I have a a 2PM, 3PM, or 04:30.
stewart_read: Rep offered concrete slots and got a time locked, but the button-up afterward skipped the one-hour-block framing and the no-driving/computer instruction entirely — only a generic "we'll probably reach out in the morning" follow-up was given.
coaching_implication: Add the standard button-up elements (hour block, no-driving-at-computer ask, explicit 'is that fair?' handshake) before ending the call — currently the appointment is locked on time only, not fully buttoned per protocol.
